survey: A simplified refracting telescope on a short tripod, standing on lunar ground. The cream tube is angled up to the right. The wider dew-shield end holds a blue objective lens facing up and toward the camera. The narrow rear end steps down through a grey collar and a gold ring to a small grey eyepiece at lower left, in line with the tube as a simple refractor's would be. A grey ring clamp holds the tube near its balance point. The clamp sits in a grey U-yoke with a visible pivot bolt on the near arm, so the tube can tilt. The far arm shows faintly behind the tube. The yoke sits on a square grey base plate, bolted on top of a round wooden tripod head. Three wooden legs fit into gold collars on the underside of that head: one at front left, one at back left and one at right. They splay evenly, and each ends in a grey rubber foot that touches the ground, with matching contact shadows. The tube is clear of the ground and the legs. Nothing floats, no parts pass through each other, and there are no loose cables or extra parts.
